name: Asmaveth
title: David's Hero from Bahurim and Overseer of the Treasuries
summary: Asmaveth is a name borne by several individuals in the Old Testament, and it is debated whether any of them are identical. The most prominent is Asmaveth of Bahurim, who was one of David's thirty mighty men – an elite force known for their individual feats in battle. Another Asmaveth, son of Adiel, served as overseer over the king's treasuries, an important administrative position in David's kingdom. In addition, Jeiel and Pelet, sons of an Asmaveth, are mentioned among the warriors who joined David at Ziklag during his time as a fugitive from King Saul. Whether the hero from Bahurim, the treasurer, and the father of Jeiel and Pelet is the same person cannot be determined from the biblical texts alone. The name also appears as a place name, Beth-Asmaveth, in connection with returnees from exile.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among David's Heroes
keyEvents.description: Asmaveth from Bahurim is listed among David's thirty mighty warriors who distinguished themselves in battle.

keyEvents.title: Listed in the Chronicles' Register of Heroes
keyEvents.description: Asmaveth from Bahurim is also mentioned in the parallel list of David's heroes in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Sons of Asmaveth Join David at Ziklag
keyEvents.description: Jeziel and Pelet, sons of an Asmaveth, were among the skilled warriors who joined David at Ziklag while he was fleeing from King Saul. It is uncertain whether this Asmaveth is identical to the hero from Bahurim.

keyEvents.title: Overseer of the King's Treasuries
keyEvents.description: Asmaveth, son of Adiel, was appointed overseer of King David's treasuries—a central administrative position. It is uncertain whether this is the same person as the hero from Bahurim.

versions.summary: Asmaveth (also called Asmaveth of Bahurim) was one of David's mighty men and trusted officials. He served as overseer of the king's treasuries. His sons were also among David's warriors, and his family was known for its loyalty to David throughout his reign.
versions.title: David's Treasurer and Warrior
versions.reason: [minor] The title is good but could be slightly refined. 'Treasurer' is a bit informal; 'overseer of the treasuries' is more precise. Alternatively, one may retain 'treasurer' for readability.; [major] It is important to distinguish between the various individuals named Asmavet in the Bible. The Asmavet who was among David's thirty mighty men (2 Sam 23:31; 1 Chr 11:33) is 'Asmavet of Bahurim' – his father is not mentioned. The Asmavet who served as overseer of the treasuries (1 Chr 27:25) is described as 'son of Adiel'. It is uncertain whether this is the same person. The profile possibly blends two (or more) different individuals with the same name. The father 'Adiel' applies to the treasurer, not necessarily to the hero from Bahurim.; [major] In 1 Chr 12:3, 'Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Asmavet', are mentioned. However, this may be a different Asmavet than either the hero from Bahurim or the treasurer. The Hebrew name Asmavet occurs for several individuals. The name forms should also be checked: in some translations the sons are called 'Jeziel' and 'Pelet' (or similar variants). 'Jesuel' should be verified.; [minor] The summary presents all references to Asmavet as if they concern one and the same person. It should be noted that the name Asmavet occurs for several individuals in the OT, and it is uncertain whether all references concern the same individual.; [minor] The role of 'treasurer' or 'administrator' is not explicitly mentioned, although this is a central function. 'Leader' is vague. Consider adding 'overseer' or 'administrator'.; [major] The final event ('The family's return after the exile') concerns the place name Asmavet/Beth-Asmavet, not the person Asmavet from David's time. Neh 7:28 and Neh 12:29 refer to a place (a village), not directly to a descendant of this person. Furthermore, bookId 15 = Ezra and bookId 16 = Nehemiah. Neh 7:28 should have bookId 16, and Neh 12:29 should also have bookId 16. The reference with bookId 15 (Ezra) chapter 12 verse 29 is incorrect – Ezra has only ten chapters. The correct reference is Neh 12:29 (bookId 16).; [critical] bookId 15 is Ezra, which has only ten chapters. Neh 12:29 should have bookId 16 (Nehemiah), not 15 (Ezra). This is a clear error in the biblical reference.; [minor] 2 Sam 23:31 is correct (bookId 10 = 2 Samuel). Verified OK.; [major] The entire event should be considered for removal or clearly marked as concerning the place name Asmavet/Beth-Asmavet, not the person. It is misleading to include it in a personal profile without clear explanation.

versions.title: David's Hero and Overseer of the Treasuries
versions.reason: [major] The profile merges information about several possibly different individuals. Father 'Adiel' refers to the treasurer (1 Chr 27:25), while the children 'Jeziel' and 'Pelet' belong to another Asmaveth (1 Chr 12:3). The hero from Bahurim has no father listed in the texts. The merging in the family field is problematic because it gives the impression that all relationships belong to one person, whereas the summary correctly points out the uncertainty. It should be clarified that the father field applies only to the treasurer, and the children apply only to Asmaveth in 1 Chr 12:3.; [critical] 2 Samuel is bookId 10, but Asmaveth of Bahurim is mentioned in 2 Sam 23:31. This matches bookId 10. However: in many biblical numbering systems, 2 Samuel is bookId 10 (1 Sam=9, 2 Sam=10). The verse matches, but note that some lists use verse 31 and others verse 32 depending on the verse division.; [minor] The role 'administrator' is in practice an overlap with 'overseer of the treasuries'. It could be replaced with something more specific like 'one of David's mighty men' to better cover his military role.; [minor] The content of this footnote is more of the type 'linguistic' or 'historical' than 'theological', since it primarily discusses the identification of different individuals with the same name. 'Historical' would have been more appropriate as a source type.; [minor] The summary is good and balanced, but the last sentence ('The family and the name were clearly associated with loyalty to David') is somewhat speculative. Loyalty to David can be documented, but 'the name' is not in itself associated with loyalty.

footnotes.text: The name Asmaveth (Hebrew: עַזְמָוֶת, 'Azmávet) likely means 'death is strong' or 'strength from death.' Some scholars interpret it as a theophoric name with an implied divine element: 'the Strong One is protection against death.'

Bahurim, the hometown of Asmaveth the hero, was a village in the tribe of Benjamin, near Jerusalem. The place is also known from the account of Shimei who cursed David (2 Sam 16:5). Its location is often identified with Ras et-Tmim, east of the Mount of Olives.

The name Asmaveth appears for several different individuals in the Old Testament: the hero from Bahurim (2 Sam 23:31), the treasurer son of Adiel (1 Chr 27:25), father of Jeiel and Pelet (1 Chr 12:3), and as a place name, Beth-Asmaveth (Neh 7:28; 12:29). Scholars debate whether any of these references concern the same person.

David's 'mighty men' (Hebrew: gibborim) formed an elite force of warriors known for their individual feats. The list in 2 Sam 23 and 1 Chr 11 likely served as a roll of honor, comparable to similar lists known from other ancient Near Eastern cultures.

The position of overseer of the treasuries (1 Chr 27:25) was one of several administrative roles in David's organization of the kingdom. The books of Chronicles describe a bureaucratic system with officials responsible for various parts of the king's property and income, indicating a relatively developed state administration.

In rabbinic tradition, David's lists of mighty men were seen as expressions of divine blessing over David's kingship. The heroes' deeds were regarded as signs of God's active presence in Israel's military victories.
